q: Elevator 基础需求包含哪些约束？（多选）
q_en: Which constraints are part of the base Elevator problem? (Select all that apply)
options: 需要实现载重、门控和紧急停止
用户可发 hall call，进入后可选目的楼层
仿真通过 step/tick 离散推进
3 部电梯服务 0-9 共 10 层
why: 基础题聚焦调度和移动模拟。载重、门、紧急停止、动态配置和 UI 都被排除。
why_en: The base elevator design focuses on three elevators, ten floors, hall and destination requests, and discrete simulation ticks.
options_en: The system must implement weight limits, door control, and emergency stop.
Users can send a hall call, and once inside pick a destination floor.
The simulation advances through discrete step/tick calls.
Three elevators serve ten floors, numbered 0 through 9.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推进仿真一个离散时间单位的方法调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: step() advances the discrete-time simulation by one tick.

optionExplanations: 载重、门控、紧急停止是真实电梯的硬件安全层，这道题只做调度仿真，不建这些部件。
hall call 加轿厢内选楼层，是整个仿真唯一的请求入口，没它就没有 pickup/destination 可调度。
把时间切成离散 tick，每次 step 只推进一步，仿真行为可预测、可复现。
3 部电梯、10 层楼把规模钉死，楼层合法性和电梯数量从一开始就有明确边界。
optionExplanations_en: Weight limits, door control, and emergency stop are hardware-safety concerns for a real elevator, but this scoped design only simulates scheduling and movement.
A hall call plus an in-cab floor pick is the only request entry point driving the simulation — without it there's nothing to schedule.
Slicing time into discrete ticks means each step advances exactly one unit, keeping the simulation predictable and reproducible.
Fixing three elevators and ten floors pins the scale, so valid-floor and elevator-count boundaries are clear from the start.
scenario: 45 分钟白板题，只实现无硬件依赖、可单元测试的纯逻辑仿真。
scenario_en: You get 45 minutes on a whiteboard, and you can only build pure logic a unit test can drive — no hardware dependencies.

q_en: What are the core entities in the Elevator design?
options: ElevatorController、Elevator、Request
Floor、Door、Sensor、Motor
Passenger、Payment、Ticket
Building、Lobby、Renderer、Viewport、Scene
why: Controller 负责任务分配和 step 推进，Elevator 管自身位置、方向和请求集合，Request 捕获楼层和类型。Floor 只是整数。
why_en: The core model is a controller coordinating elevators, each elevator owning movement state, and requests carrying floor and type.

options_en: ElevatorController, Elevator, and Request.
Floor, Door, Sensor, and Motor.
Passenger, Payment, and Ticket.
Building, Lobby, Renderer, Viewport, and Scene.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装一次停靠请求的类，包含楼层号和请求类型两个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Request object bundles a floor number together with a request type.

optionExplanations: 这三类刚好覆盖调度协调、单梯运动状态和请求身份三件事，是这道题真正要建的模型。
楼层、门、传感器、马达都是硬件控制层，这道题范围内没有门控和传动部件，不需要建类。
乘客、计费、票据是电商或购票系统的实体，跟电梯调度和移动无关。
楼宇外壳、渲染、视口和场景图都是 UI 呈现层，这道题只考调度逻辑，不建展示对象。
optionExplanations_en: These three classes are exactly enough to cover fleet coordination, one elevator's motion state, and request identity.
Floor, door, sensor, and motor are hardware-control concerns, and this scoped problem has no doors or drive parts to model.
Passenger, payment, and ticket are entities from a booking or billing system, unrelated to elevator scheduling.
Building shell, renderer, viewport, and scene graph are UI presentation concerns; this problem only covers scheduling logic.
scenario: 电梯仿真范围只有调度与移动，不建模门、乘客身份或计费。

scenario_en: In scope, a floor is only a position; it has no state, rules, or lifecycle.

q_en: How should Floor be modeled?
options: 包含乘客队列和门状态的类
int 楼层号
Elevator 的子类
RequestType 枚举值
why: 当前范围里 floor 不维护任何状态，只是坐标。把它建成类会增加无用间接层。
why_en: Floor remains an integer because it has no state or behavior in the scoped problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果后续要建模楼层按钮、显示屏、门厅传感器或无障碍区域，Floor 才可能成为实体。
options_en: A class holding a passenger queue and door state.
A plain int floor number.
A subclass of Elevator.
A RequestType enum value.
tradeoff: int 原语 vs 独立 Floor 类

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

optionExplanations: 楼层要真的管乘客队列和门状态时才值得建类，本题范围没有门控，这个类会是空壳。
本题里楼层只是坐标，没有状态或行为，用 int 就够，也让 Request 和 Elevator 直接持有它。
楼层不是电梯的特化版本，继承关系在语义上就错了。
RequestType 表达的是请求种类，把位置塞进枚举会把楼层和请求类型混成一件事。
optionExplanations_en: A Floor class earns its keep only once it owns a passenger queue or door state; in this scope it would stay an empty shell.
Floor is nothing but a coordinate here, so a plain int is enough and lets Request or Elevator hold it directly.
A floor isn't a specialized elevator, so an inheritance relationship is semantically wrong.
RequestType encodes the kind of request, not a location — folding floor into it conflates two different things.

q: RequestType 需要区分哪些类型？（多选）
q_en: Which request types does RequestType need to distinguish? (Select all that apply)
options: PICKUP_UP
IDLE
DESTINATION
PICKUP_DOWN
why: hall call 有方向，destination 是轿厢内按钮，不带方向。IDLE 属于 Elevator 的 Direction，不是请求类型。
why_en: RequestType distinguishes up pickups, down pickups, and destination stops, while IDLE belongs to elevator direction.
options_en: PICKUP_UP for an up hall call.
IDLE for no active request.
DESTINATION for an in-cab floor button.
PICKUP_DOWN for a down hall call.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了上行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_UP is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the up button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了下行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_DOWN is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the down button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轿厢内乘客按下的目的楼层请求，不带方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DESTINATION is an in-cab floor request that carries no direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

optionExplanations: 楼层外呼叫必须带方向，PICKUP_UP 让向上电梯才去接这个人。
IDLE 描述的是电梯自己有没有请求、要不要动，属于 Direction 而不是请求种类。
轿厢内按下的目的楼层不带方向，到达即服务，所以单独算一种类型。
同理，PICKUP_DOWN 让下行电梯去接，不会被上行电梯错误接走。
optionExplanations_en: A hall call needs a direction, and PICKUP_UP makes sure only an up-moving elevator answers it.
IDLE describes whether the elevator itself has work to do, so it belongs to Direction, not to request type.
An in-cab destination has no direction — the elevator just serves it on arrival, so it gets its own type.
Symmetrically, PICKUP_DOWN routes the pickup to a down-moving elevator instead of an upward one.
scenario: SCAN 调度只沿当前方向服务，Controller 要从请求本身判断它顺不顺路。
scenario_en: SCAN dispatch only serves stops along the current direction, so the controller has to tell from the request itself whether it is on the way.

scenario: 电梯在 5 楼向上，已有 7、8 楼请求；7 楼有人按 DOWN。
scenario_en: The elevator is on floor 5 moving up with requests at floors 7 and 8; someone on floor 7 presses DOWN.
q: 为什么只用 Set<Integer> 存楼层不够？
q_en: Why is Set<Integer> not enough for pending floors?
options: 楼层号不能比较大小
Set<Integer> 根本没法对同一楼层去重
无法区分 7 楼向上停靠和 7 楼向下接人
目的楼层不能用整数表示
why: 同一楼层不同请求类型语义不同。向上的电梯不应为了 PICKUP_DOWN 在 7 楼停下接错方向乘客。
why_en: A floor-only request loses whether a hall call is for up or down pickup.
whenOtherWins: 初级或极简模拟可以只存楼层，只要承认会有方向体验问题。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  F["floor 7"] --> U["PICKUP_UP"]
  F --> D["PICKUP_DOWN"]
  U --> A["up elevator may stop"]
  D --> B["down elevator may stop"]
options_en: Floor numbers cannot be compared for ordering.
Set<Integer> cannot deduplicate entries for the same floor.
It cannot distinguish an up-bound stop at floor 7 from a down pickup at floor 7.
A destination floor cannot be represented as an integer.
tradeoff: Set<Integer> vs Set<Request>

termDefinitions.meaning: 只存楼层号的集合，无法区分同楼层不同方向的请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Set<Integer> stores only floor numbers and cannot distinguish same-floor requests of different direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储 Request 对象的集合，用楼层加类型共同判重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Set<Request> stores Request objects and de-duplicates using floor plus type together.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了上行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_UP is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the up button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了下行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_DOWN is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the down button on a floor.

optionExplanations: 整数天然可比较大小，排序和距离计算都没问题，这不是失败点。
Set 恰恰会去重——问题在于它把 7 楼两个不同方向的请求错误合并成一个。
同一楼层的上行停靠和下行接人是两件事，只存楼层号会把它们混成一条记录。
目的楼层照样能用整数表示，这不是本题真正的限制。
optionExplanations_en: Integers compare fine for ordering and distance, so that isn't the actual failure.
A Set does deduplicate — the real issue is it wrongly merges two different-direction requests at floor 7 into one.
An up-bound stop and a down pickup at the same floor 7 are two different things a floor-only entry can't tell apart.
A destination floor is still perfectly representable as an integer, so that isn't the real limitation.

scenario_en: When an elevator has no pending requests, it should not keep drifting up or down.
q: Direction enum 为什么需要 IDLE？
q_en: Why does the Direction enum need IDLE?
options: 表示电梯故障
表示 hall call 的向上按钮
表示目的楼层
表示无请求不移动的状态
why: UP/DOWN 只能表示运动方向，不能表达静止。IDLE 让 step 在无请求时自然停住。
why_en: IDLE represents an elevator with no active movement, preventing it from drifting forever.
whenOtherWins: 如果用 nullable direction 或状态机对象，也能表达 idle，但 enum 更简单。
options_en: It represents an elevator malfunction.
It represents the up button of a hall call.
It represents a destination floor.
It represents the no-requests, not-moving state.
tradeoff: IDLE 枚举值 vs nullable direction

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

optionExplanations: 故障应该用单独的错误状态或字段表达，混进 Direction 会让正常和异常判断纠缠。
上行按钮的方向属于 hall call 的 RequestType，不该塞进电梯自身的运动方向。
目的楼层是 Request 里的一个字段，不是电梯的运动方向。
UP/DOWN 只能表达在动，电梯没请求时需要一个显式的静止值，否则 step 无法收敛。
optionExplanations_en: A malfunction deserves its own error state or field — folding it into Direction blurs normal and abnormal cases.
The up-button direction belongs to the hall call's RequestType, not to the elevator's own movement state.
A destination floor is a field on Request, not a direction the elevator moves in.
UP/DOWN can only describe motion, so an elevator with no requests needs an explicit still value or step never settles.

q_en: Which state should an Elevator store? (Select all that apply)

direction

options_en: currentFloor, its own position.
direction, its own movement state.
The positions of other elevators.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储 Request 对象的集合，用楼层加类型共同判重。

optionExplanations: 每次移动和边界检查都要知道自己在哪层，这是最基本的状态。
UP/DOWN/IDLE 决定该不该反向、该不该停，缺了它 step 无法判断下一步。
全局视图属于 Controller 的职责，单部电梯知道别的电梯位置会打破封装边界。
自己的待服务请求集合决定它下一步往哪走、在哪停，是这台电梯的核心待办清单。

UP/DOWN/IDLE decides whether to reverse or stop, so step can't make its next move without it.
Fleet-wide visibility is the controller's job; letting one elevator know others' positions breaks encapsulation.
Its own pending-request set is what decides where it heads next and where it stops — this elevator's to-do list.
scenario: 3 部电梯各自 step 推进，每部只能读写自己的字段，避免状态互相污染。
scenario_en: The three elevators each advance their own step, and one may only read and write its own fields so their state does not bleed into each other.

q: 这个决策应该放在哪里？
q_en: Where should this dispatch decision live?
options: ElevatorController
单个 Elevator 内部逻辑
Request 的构造函数中
Floor 这个类里
why: 调度需要看多部电梯的全局状态，因此属于 Controller。单个 Elevator 不应该知道其他电梯。
why_en: Dispatch belongs in ElevatorController because it requires fleet-level information.
whenOtherWins: 单电梯系统可以直接给该 Elevator.addRequest，省掉 Controller 调度逻辑。
options_en: ElevatorController.
Inside a single Elevator's own logic.
Inside the Request constructor.
Inside the Floor class.
tradeoff: 全局调度决策 vs 单电梯本地状态

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装一次停靠请求的类，包含楼层号和请求类型两个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Request object bundles a floor number together with a request type.

optionExplanations: 派发要比较所有电梯的状态才能选出最合适的一部，只有 Controller 拿得到这个全局视角。
单部电梯只认识自己的楼层和请求，让它比较别的电梯会破坏封装边界。
构造函数应该只负责校验和初始化字段，不该在创建对象时顺带做调度决策。

A single elevator only knows its own floor and requests — asking it to compare others breaks the encapsulation boundary.
A constructor should just validate and initialize fields, not sneak in a fleet-wide dispatch decision.

scenario_en: requestElevator is the hall-call API, and it accepts only up or down hall calls.
q: 为什么参数用 RequestType 而不是 Direction？
q_en: Why should the API parameter use RequestType instead of Direction?
options: Direction 不能表示上行方向
RequestType 排除 IDLE 值
RequestType 会自动选择电梯
Direction 类型无法做相等比较
why: hall call 不可能是 IDLE。使用更窄的类型减少运行时校验和非法状态。
why_en: Using RequestType for hall calls avoids accepting IDLE as a valid request direction.
whenOtherWins: 内部电梯运动状态仍应使用 Direction，因为它确实需要 IDLE。
options_en: Direction cannot represent the up direction.
RequestType excludes IDLE at the type level.
RequestType automatically selects an elevator.
Direction values cannot be compared for equality.
tradeoff: RequestType 参数 vs Direction 参数

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

optionExplanations: Direction 里明明有 UP，这不是问题所在。
hall call 永远带方向，用 RequestType 能在类型层面就排除 IDLE 这个非法输入，不用运行时再校验。
参数类型只负责表达合法输入，真正选哪部电梯仍由 Controller 的调度逻辑决定。
枚举之间的相等比较没有问题，这不是选类型的理由。
optionExplanations_en: Direction clearly includes UP, so that isn't the actual problem.
A hall call is never IDLE, so typing the parameter as RequestType rules out that illegal value at compile time instead of a runtime check.

q: 这段 helper 的作用是什么？
q_en: What does this helper check?
codeSample:
hasRequestsAtOrBeyond(floor, dir)
    for request in requests
        if dir == UP && request.floor >= floor
            if request.type == PICKUP_UP || request.type == DESTINATION
                return true
        if dir == DOWN && request.floor <= floor
            if request.type == PICKUP_DOWN || request.type == DESTINATION
                return true
    return false

确认队列会把电梯带到或越过请求楼层
判断当前楼层是否越界

q: FIFO 移动策略的主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem with FIFO movement?
options: 它在任何请求分布下都能走最短总距离
它需要预先知道全部请求才能排序
严格按到达顺序服务会来回折返

It needs to know every request up front before it can order them.
Serving strictly in arrival order makes the elevator thrash back and forth.
It avoids the overhead of maintaining a request queue at all.

FIFO 只看到达先后，来一个排一个，根本不做排序，也不需要提前知道全部请求。
严格按到达顺序服务会让电梯像 8→3→7 这样来回折返，乘客感觉被无视。

It still reverses direction for the nearest request, so passengers watch the elevator leave then come back.
